faq.q: Can I bring my own gluten-free food and drinks on board?
faq.a: Absolutely. You are welcome to bring any gluten-free food and drinks you like. The only restriction is glass bottles (for safety on deck). Use cans or plastic containers instead. Most boats have a fridge or cool box where you can store perishable items.

faq.q: Are the standard drinks and snacks included in the charter gluten-free?
faq.a: Yes, our standard inclusions – bottled water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava – are naturally gluten-free. However, the light snacks provided (typically crisps or nuts) may vary. If you have coeliac disease, please bring your own snacks to be safe.

faq.q: Where can I buy gluten-free food near Puerto Banús?
faq.a: Mercadona on Avenida del Prado and Carrefour in the Puerto Banús shopping centre both have dedicated gluten-free sections. You can buy bread, pasta, crackers, and even frozen gluten-free pizzas. For fresh gluten-free pastries, try La Coquette bakery in Marbella town.

faq.q: Do any of your boats have a galley or kitchen?
faq.a: Yes, larger yachts like the Mangusta 80, Azimut 58 Flybridge, and Ferretti 94 have a well-equipped galley with a fridge, hob, and microwave. Smaller boats like the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 have a small fridge and sink. You can prepare simple gluten-free meals onboard.

faq.q: Can I request a gluten-free meal to be arranged in advance?
faq.a: We do not provide catering directly, but we can recommend local catering companies that offer gluten-free options. Just let us know at least 48 hours before your charter, and we will connect you with a trusted supplier.

faq.q: What gluten-free foods are easiest to pack for a boat trip?
faq.a: Think portable and non-perishable: gluten-free wraps, rice cakes, crackers, nuts, dried fruit, pre-cooked quinoa or rice salads, canned tuna, hummus, and gluten-free granola bars. Fresh fruit like apples and bananas are also great. Avoid anything that crumbles easily.

faq.q: Is there a risk of cross-contamination on the boat?
faq.a: If you bring your own sealed, labelled food and use separate utensils and plates (which we can provide), the risk is very low. The galley surfaces are wiped down, but we recommend bringing a clean chopping board or tray to prepare your food on.

faq.q: Can I bring my own gluten-free beer?
faq.a: Yes, gluten-free beer is welcome. Cans are preferred over bottles for safety. Brands like Daura Damm, Estrella Galicia Sin Gluten, and Ambar Especial Sin Gluten are widely available in Marbella supermarkets.

data.body_html:
Planning a marbella boat rental what to bring food gluten free checklist is essential for coeliacs and gluten-intolerant guests. While our standard inclusions – bottled water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava – are naturally gluten-free, the light snacks provided may not be. Bringing your own safe food ensures a worry-free day on the water. This guide covers what to pack, where to buy gluten-free provisions near Puerto Banús, and how to handle cross-contamination on board.

What Our Standard Inclusions Contain (Gluten-Free Check)

Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and a selection of drinks and snacks. The drinks are all gluten-free: still and sparkling water, soft drinks (Coca-Cola, Sprite, tonic), gluten-free beer, white wine, and cava. The snacks are usually crisps or salted nuts – check the label if you are highly sensitive. For a safe option, bring your own sealed gluten-free crackers or rice cakes.

Gluten-Free Food Checklist for Your Boat Day

Pack smart for a day on the Mediterranean. Here is a practical list of gluten-free foods that travel well:

  • Wraps & bread: gluten-free tortillas, baguettes, or pitta – fill with ham, cheese, or hummus.
  • Salads: quinoa, rice, or pasta salad (pre-made at home) – keep cool in a small cooler bag.
  • Protein: canned tuna, pre-cooked chicken strips, hard-boiled eggs, or smoked salmon.
  • Snacks: nuts, dried fruit, gluten-free crackers, popcorn, rice cakes, and fruit (apples, bananas, grapes).
  • Sweet treats: gluten-free brownies, biscuits, or chocolate – avoid anything with crumbly coatings.
  • Drinks: extra gluten-free beer (cans only), fruit juices, and plenty of water.

Where to Buy Gluten-Free Food Near Puerto Banús

Marbella has excellent gluten-free shopping options. The Mercadona on Avenida del Prado has a dedicated 'Sin Gluten' section with bread, pasta, crackers, and frozen products. Carrefour in the Puerto Banús shopping centre also stocks a wide range. For fresh gluten-free pastries, visit La Coquette bakery in Marbella town (Calle Nuestra Señora de los Dolores). If you need a quick fix, the El Corte Inglés supermarket in Marbella has a good selection too.

How to Avoid Cross-Contamination on Board

All our yachts are cleaned between charters, but galley surfaces may have trace gluten. Bring your own clean chopping board, utensils, and paper towels. Use separate plates and cutlery for your gluten-free food. If you have severe coeliac disease, inform your skipper in advance – they can wipe down the galley with a clean cloth. Larger yachts like the Mangusta 80 and Azimut 58 Flybridge have spacious galleys where you can prepare food safely.

Best Boat Choices for Gluten-Free Guests

If you plan to cook or prepare food onboard, yachts with a full galley are ideal. The Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) has a well-equipped kitchen with hob and microwave. The Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) offers a professional-grade galley. For smaller groups, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) has a compact fridge and sink – perfect for storing pre-prepared gluten-free meals. All depart from Puerto Banús, so you can shop en route.

Gluten-Free Dining Options Near Marbella Marinas

If you prefer to eat ashore, several restaurants near Puerto Banús cater to gluten-free diets. El Chiringuito on the Golden Mile has a gluten-free menu (grilled fish, salads). Bibo by Dani García offers gluten-free tapas (book ahead). La Pesquera in Puerto Banús serves gluten-free paella on request. Always confirm with the chef before ordering – coeliac safety is taken seriously here.

What to Do If You Forget Something

Forgot your gluten-free crackers? No problem. Most supermercados in Marbella deliver to Puerto Banús via apps like Glovo or Uber Eats. You can order gluten-free bread, snacks, and drinks within 30 minutes. Alternatively, ask your skipper to stop at a chiringuito along the coast – many serve gluten-free options. The key is to communicate your needs in advance so we can help you have a safe, enjoyable day.
